rounds.fact: Answers.com built its early traffic by aggregating dictionary, encyclopedia, and reference content into a single searchable site, well before crowdsourced Q&A sites took over that space.
Priceline's original pitch was a 'name your own price' auction system for flights and hotels, an unusual model that made it one of the most talked-about dot-com startups of its era.
Photobucket became the default way millions of MySpace users hosted images for their profiles, since MySpace itself didn't offer easy photo uploading in its early years.
Wikipedia's interface has stayed remarkably close to its original look for two decades. The visual restraint was intentional, to keep the focus on editing and content rather than design.
LimeWire became one of the most popular peer-to-peer file-sharing programs after Napster's shutdown, before being forced offline itself by a 2010 court injunction.
